title: Fancy_Bear_Incident_Response_Scenario_b24
description: This scenario simulates an incident involving Fancy Bear malware on your network. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Fancy Bear, also known as APT29, is a sophisticated cyber espionage group known for targeting government, military, and corporate networks. This scenario simulates an incident involving Fancy Bear malware on your network. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have access to the `target` host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: Users have reported slow network performance. Investigate the `target` host to identify any suspicious network activity. Submit the port number of the suspicious service running on the system.
levels.solution: Check running services and network connections. The suspicious service is running on port 4444.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network performance issues can often be caused by unusual or unauthorized services running on the system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check running services and network connections to identify any suspicious activity.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all running services and their associated ports.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is maintained on the system. Investigate the persistence mechanism used by the service. Submit the name of the systemd timer responsible for the suspicious service.
levels.solution: Check systemd services and timers. The systemd timer responsible for the suspicious service is `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms are used by attackers to maintain access to a compromised system, often through scheduled tasks or services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check systemd services and timers to identify any persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Check if the attacker has moved laterally to other hosts in the network. Investigate any file transfers or remote execution activities from the `target` host. Submit the name of the service responsible for transferring files to the `next-target` host.
levels.solution: Check logs and systemd services related to file transfers. The service responsible for transferring files to the `next-target` host is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Lateral movement involves attackers moving from one compromised system to another within the same network, often through file transfers or remote execution.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check logs and systemd services related to file transfers to identify any lateral movement.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all systemd services.
